input.label: How are the individuals who are the focus of the project to be selected?
input.hint:
This might be a group of people born after a particular date, or people in contact with a particular agency during a specific period.
If you are interested in more than one group of people, you will receive a single collection of data containing all groups.
You will need to outline how the overall group will be identified, and how you will divide these into the separate groups of interest as part of the analysis.

input.label: ## Cohort selection
input.hint:
Selection of individuals can be based on the primary event date of the dataset, age or birth date, sex, or geographic areas (specifically those based on the the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
Using your description of the people to be investigated, list the datasets and variables that will be used to identify these individuals.
If you are using multiple rules to identify the group or groups of individuals, please add a comment to advise how these rules should interact with each other.
In the following section, select a dataset, variable, and filter expression that captures your group. You can add as many as you need, but we recommend up to four.

select1.label: Dataset
select1.hint: Choose a dataset that contains your target individuals.

select1.label: Variable
select1.hint: Choose a variable that filters the dataset to the target individual.

input.label: Filter expression
input.hint: Specify a filter value.

input.label: Geographic area
input.hint: Draw the area which includes geolocations of the target events or individuals.

input.label: Comment
input.hint: Add any useful explanations or clarifications.

select1.label: Filter combination
select1.hint: Specify whether the target individuals MUST occur in this selection (i.e., if not present in this selection but in others, they will be excluded), or CAN occur in this selection (i.e., if not present in this selection but in others, they will be included).

input.label: Geocoding can be requested for many of the datasets listed below using one of our two standard packages based on the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) published [here](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/latest-release). Geocoding for the specific areas listed in each package will be provided in a separate data table.
input.hint: Additional geographic areas in the ASGS can be derived by using mapping tables to directly map up to larger geographic areas (e.g. SA2 to SA4) or concordances files to approximate the mapping between different unrelated areas (e.g. SA2 to Indigenous Areas).
